title: Galangin alleviates vascular aging and endothelial cell senescence by targeting SMAD3 to initiate mitophagy.
authors: Ding, Xiao-Qing; Li, Ke-Xin; Liu, Jing-Wen; Zhang, Rui-En; Lei, Chun-Ran; Saqirile; Yi, Zi-Xin; Li, Ke; Liu, Peng-Xia; Yang, Rui; Wang, Chang-Shan
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究黄酮类化合物Galangin通过靶向SMAD3调控线粒体自噬缓解血管衰老，虽涉及分子对接和MD模拟及ChIP验证SMAD3-DNA结合，但核心是药物-蛋白互作而非TF-DNA结合机制建模，与课题关联有限。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Senescence of vascular endothelial cells (ECs) plays a critical role in cardiovascular diseases. Galangin (3,5,7-Trihydroxyflavone) is a flavonoid derived from plants and medicinal herbs with various biological activities. However, its effect on endothelial cell senescence and the underlying molecular mechanisms are poorly characterised. PURPOSE: This study aimed to evaluate the therapeutic effects of Galangin on endothelial cell senescence and vascular aging, providing a theoretical basis for its clinical application. METHODS: Human aortic endothelial cells and mice were treated with d-galactose to induce senescence. The expression levels of aging markers beta-galactosidase, P21, P53, and gamma-H2AX were detected using western blot. Cell proliferation was determined using CCK-8 assays. Network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations were used to identify Galangin downstream targets. MST, CETSA, and DARTS assays were used to determine the binding of Galangin to SMAD3 protein. ROS levels were measured using flow cytometry. JC-1 staining was used to determine mitochondrial membrane potential. Mitophagy-related markers Parkin, PINK1, LC3, and P62 were detected using western blot and immunohistochemistry. ChIP assay was used to determine p-SMAD3's effect on the downstream genes PINK1 and LC3. RESULTS: Our pioneering study reveals a novel protective role of Galangin in vascular aging, primarily through a newly identified mechanism: activating mitophagy by targeting SMAD3. Notably, Galangin directly binds to SMAD3 and promotes the transcriptional regulation of PINK1 and LC3. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings demonstrate the protective effect of Galangin in vascular aging and hold promising prospects for both clinical application and future research.
abstract_zh: 背景：血管内皮细胞（ECs）的衰老在心血管疾病中发挥关键作用。高良姜素（3,5,7-三羟基黄酮）是一种源自植物和药用草本的类黄酮，具有多种生物活性。然而，其对内皮细胞衰老的影响及潜在分子机制尚不清楚。目的：本研究旨在评估高良姜素对内皮细胞衰老和血管老化的治疗作用，为其临床应用提供理论基础。方法：使用d-半乳糖处理人主动脉内皮细胞和小鼠以诱导衰老。通过western blot检测衰老标志物β-半乳糖苷酶、P21、P53和γ-H2AX的表达水平。使用CCK-8实验测定细胞增殖。采用网络药理学、分子对接和分子动力学模拟来识别高良姜素的下游靶点。使用MST、CETSA和DARTS实验确定高良姜素与SMAD3蛋白的结合。通过流式细胞术测量ROS水平。使用JC-1染色测定线粒体膜电位。通过western blot和免疫组化检测线粒体自噬相关标志物Parkin、PINK1、LC3和P62。使用ChIP实验确定p-SMAD3对下游基因PINK1和LC3的影响。结果：我们的开创性研究揭示了高良姜素在血管老化中的新型保护作用，主要通过一种新识别的机制：通过靶向SMAD3激活线粒体自噬。值得注意的是，高良姜素直接结合SMAD3并促进PINK1和LC3的转录调控。结论：我们的研究结果证明了高良姜素在血管老化中的保护作用，并为其临床应用和未来研究展现了广阔前景。
